strings.name: Tristan Harris
strings.role: Co-Founder and President, Center for Humane Technology
strings.summary: American technology ethics advocate Tristan Harris cofounded and led Apture and worked on design ethics at Google. With colleagues, he uses CHT, podcasts and documentaries to discuss platform design, the attention economy and AI governance; his risk assessments are advocacy positions.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth remains uncertain between 1983 and 1984. President is distinct from executive director; the 2026 board transition announcement is not proof every step is complete.
strings.influence.rationale: Cofounded the Center for Humane Technology, advancing public discussion of social platform design, the attention economy and AI impacts.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Stanford computer science undergraduate, identified as class of 2006; studied persuasive technology. Graduate study is not a completed masters degree.
strings.facts.f2.label: Podcast co-host
strings.facts.f2.value: Hosts Your Undivided Attention with Aza Raskin, discussing technology incentives and social impacts.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Platform incentives
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advocates assessing technology’s contribution to life beyond time spent; specific causal and risk claims require evidence.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Public communication and AI governance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses documentaries, podcasts and briefings to advance discussion; team achievements and film awards are not solely his.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Organization announces strategy change
strings.timeline.t1.text: CHT’s board announces founder-led communication and decision-maker engagement, scaling back internal research, policy and litigation programs; not Harris’s individual decision.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Podcast on AI and human dignity
strings.timeline.t2.text: Episode 137 with Raskin discusses AI governance and a Vatican visit; date is publication, not an inferred meeting date.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Appears in The Social Dilemma
strings.timeline.t3.text: Documentary participant discussing social platforms’ business models and design; film awards are not personal awards.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-launches Center for Humane Technology
strings.timeline.t4.text: Launches CHT with Aza Raskin and Randima Fernando; institutional launch year does not establish legal incorporation date.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Stanford publishes technology ethics talk
strings.timeline.t5.text: University publishes Making Technology Less Manipulative, presenting his Time Well Spent cofounder role and design advocacy.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Calls for respect for attention
strings.timeline.t6.text: Creates an internal Google presentation on reducing distraction and respecting users’ attention, prompting design ethics discussion.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Google acquires Apture
strings.timeline.t7.text: Team announces move to Chrome; price undisclosed, with no inferred personal proceeds or immediate design ethicist title.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Cofounds Apture
strings.timeline.t8.text: Forms company with Can Sar and Jesse Young as CEO, developing contextual information and multimedia tools within webpages.
